reuse.why: Holidays are threaded through the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend, but getDatesInRange re-derives the daily-skip rule and the weekend-or-holiday test instead of reusing getNextDate's logic or exporting isNonWorkingDay.

duplication.why: The daily weekend/holiday skip now lives both in getNextDate and in getDatesInRange (with `d.isWeekend(date) || isHoliday(...)` restating isNonWorkingDay), while schedule-template and getUpcomingDates keep their own skipWeekend ternaries.

placement.why: Holiday and weekend-adjust rules sit in shared/schedules.ts and the range handler beside getUpcomingDates in server/schedules/app.ts, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes are on-task across the four steps; the occurrence-window hack (take: Math.max(7, holidays.length + 7)) and mixed reading of holidays from dateCond.value vs schedule.data add noise.

maintainability.why: The daily-skip rule is applied in getNextDate and getDatesInRange but not in getUpcomingDates or schedule-template's own adjustment, so the weekend rule is now decided differently per path and future changes must find every copy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts and schedule-template.ts createScheduleList apply weekend handling themselves around getDateWithSkippedWeekend instead of through one shared 'final date of an occurrence' function.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange reshapes getNextDate's daily skip (skipWeekend && frequency === 'daily' && non-working day) into a flatMap filter and inlines isNonWorkingDay as d.isWeekend || isHoliday.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a skipsDailyWeekends branch (widened occurrence window + filter) and a !skipsDailyWeekends guard on the adjust; getDatesInRange, getUpcomingDates and schedule-template's createScheduleList decide weekend handling outside getNextDate.
